title: Number of output files created in s3 after Spark Partitioning
question:
Recently, during in an interview I faced below question which made me scratching my head and I still don't have the proper answer to it. So please bare with me.

Let's say I a pyspark dataframe having 20 partitions, out of that
only 4 has data in it and 16 are empty. 
Now, if this dataframe is saved to s3 or any other object store how many part files will be created?

I responded since there are 20 partitions so 4 part-files having data and 16 part files with no data in them will be created in s3.

To this a followup question came, lets say the same dataframe is using paritionBy or repartitioned then used paritionBy and saved as below -

Scenario 1. df.paritionBy("col5").write.format("parquet").save("s3_path_1")

Here, I responded that based upon the column values in col5 hierarchical directory structure will be maintained in the s3 bucket. So the number of part files in each one of the directories will be between 1 and 4 as there are 4 partitions with data in them.

Scenario 2. df.repartition(5).partitionBy("col5").write.format("parquet").save("s3_path_2")

In this scenario, I responded that since we're repartitioning the dataframe so the number of part-files within each directory on s3 will be between 1 and 5 as the data is re-distributed amongst 5 partitions.

In either of my responses, interviewer doesn't seem to have convinced. Am I missing anything here?
answer:
I think ( and based on little experiment i did locally) you were right on partitonBy that it creates folder .

Let's say I a pyspark dataframe having 20 partitions, out of that
only 4 has data in it and 16 are empty. 
Now, if this dataframe is saved to s3 or any other object store how many part files will be created?

For the number of part files in above scenario though answer will be 4 files will be created as the tasks with no data will not create the files.

Scenario 1. df.paritionBy("col5").write.format("parquet").save("s3_path_1")

For the scenario 1., for the part files again it really depends on how the shuffling is done, what kind of setting we have (AQE Enabled, maxRecordsPerFile configuration, etc..). But if we consider the data is very small and initial partition is 4 , if there are records present with col5 , it could be anywhere between 1 to max no.of records present per col5 value.



 val schema = StructType(Seq(
   StructField("id", IntegerType, nullable = false),
   StructField("value", StringType, nullable = false)
 ))

 val data = Seq(
   (1, "A"), (2, "B"), (3, "C"), (4, "D"),
   (2, "E"), (6, "F"), (3, "G"), (3, "H")
 )


 val rdd = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(data, 4)

 val df = spark.createDataFrame(rdd.map(Row.fromTuple), schema)


 df.write.format("parquet")
   .mode("overwrite")
   .partitionBy("id")
   .option("checkpointLocation", "/Users/vg/Documents/testpartition3")
   .save("/tmp/save_as_parquet")

In the above example , there are 4 partitions with data when partitionBy is called. For the value 3 there are 3 values but the no.of part files created is 2. It is not because there are no. of four partitions with data. It is because the no.of records for value 3 is 3 so the no.of files will be anywhere between 1 to 3.

Scenario 2. df.repartition(5).partitionBy("col5").write.format("parquet").save("s3_path_2")

For the scenario 2. although there are 20 tasks it acts the same as way as the initial question. Tasks that have no data will not create the part file. So it will end up anywhere between 1 to no.of records per col5 . Here, since there are more tasks already created i have observed no.of files created are more . i.e for id=3 3 part files are created instead of 2.

Hope this helps. More than happy to discuss further since this is something i had to try out as well to confirm my answer.
